nodes.description: The mechanistic core. Mutant tropoelastin self-associates more readily than normal, so its coacervation temperature is lower, and in an equimolar mixture with wild-type protein the mixture behaves like the mutant alone. That dominance at the level of coacervation is the molecular basis of the dominant inheritance. The mutant also binds fibrillin-1 and fibulin-5 poorly, so tropoelastin aggregates into elastin-only globules instead of being laid down on microfibrils and cross-linked by lysyl oxidase; the result is less mature, insoluble elastin. Both halves of the defect, increased aggregation and decreased microfibril binding, are needed to explain the poor integration of elastin into fibres.

nodes.description: The initiating lesion. Most patients carry a single-nucleotide deletion or small duplication in exons 30 to 34 of ELN, the last exons of the gene, with a recurrent hotspot at c.2262delA in exon 32. Because the frameshift sits so close to the end of the coding sequence, it does not remove the protein; it replaces the normal carboxy terminus of tropoelastin with a missense peptide that reads through into the 3' untranslated region. Exceptions exist, a splice-site allele and a partial tandem duplication, but they converge on the same abnormal C-terminal product. This is what distinguishes the disease from supravalvular aortic stenosis, where ELN alleles are null.

nodes.description: The signalling amplifier. Fibroblasts from every patient studied show increased phospho-SMAD2, and the transgenic mouse lung shows elevated TGF-beta signalling markers alongside decreased stiffness and increased stretch at physiological pressure. The proposed logic is borrowed from Marfan syndrome: microfibrils sequester latent TGF-beta, a compliant matrix releases more of it under load, and excess TGF-beta drives the medial disorganisation and failed alveolar septation that show up as aortic root dilatation and emphysema. This is the node that makes ADCL1 a member of the heritable aortopathy family, and it is the only node with a proposed drug target, losartan, which has never been tried in this disease.

nodes.description: The consequence in the tissues whose job is to spring back. Skin stretched by growth, gravity and expression does not return, so it hangs in redundant folds and the face ages prematurely; the eyelid skin droops into ptosis and blepharochalasis; the abdominal wall and inguinal canal yield to hernias; the joints are hyperlax in infancy; the vocal folds lose tension and the voice is hoarse or husky; and the bladder wall gives way to diverticula. All of these are the same lesion read in different elastic-fibre-rich tissues.

nodes.description: Rhytidectomy, blepharoplasty for ptosis and staged excision of redundant skin improve appearance and function, and are what most patients actually receive. The elastic-fibre defect persists, so recurrence within months is the rule in the older literature; a multi-step, sequential surgical plan is now advocated, and one recent patient remained recurrence-free at five months. Recorded as symptomatic: the operation removes lax skin, it does not act on any node of the mechanism.

nodes.description: The mutant message survives. Whether a given transcript is degraded depends on where the frameshift falls relative to alternative splicing: exon 32 is naturally skipped in about 70% of fibroblast transcripts, so a mutation inside it is spliced out of most messages and the phenotype is milder, while mutations in exons 30, 33 and 34 remain in the message whatever the splice pattern. Alternative splicing is therefore the best-understood modifier of severity in this disease, and the reason the same molecular class produces such a range of organ involvement.

nodes.description: Fibroblasts and other elastogenic cells make the mutant tropoelastin and export most of it. This is the step that makes the disease dominant negative rather than haploinsufficient: an abnormal protein reaches the extracellular space in quantity and is available to interfere with assembly. Part of it is retained intracellularly, and that fraction feeds the endoplasmic reticulum stress branch below. The carboxy terminus that is lost normally mediates binding to microfibril-associated glycoproteins and cell-surface glycosaminoglycans, both required for elastic fibre formation.
